question: Which of the following about phenytoin is true ?

options.opc: It is excreted unchanged in urine

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Phenytoin is a medication" -> "It is primarily metabolized by the liver" -> "It follows Michaelis-Menten kinetics at therapeutic doses" -> "At high doses, it exhibits zero order kinetics" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Phenytoin induces hepatic enzymes" -> "It increases the metabolism of other drugs" -> "It is classified as an enzyme inducer" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Phenytoin is metabolized in the liver" -> "Only a small fraction is excreted unchanged in urine" -> "Most is excreted as metabolites" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Phenytoin is known to cause fetal harm" -> "It is classified as teratogenic" -> "It can lead to fetal hydantoin syndrome" -> 95%
analysis: Phenytoin is known to follow zero-order kinetics at therapeutic doses, meaning that its elimination rate is constant regardless of the concentration in the blood. It is also a hepatic enzyme inducer, particularly of CYP450 enzymes. Phenytoin is not excreted unchanged in urine; rather, it is metabolized in the liver. Additionally, phenytoin is teratogenic and can cause fetal hydantoin syndrome when taken during pregnancy. Therefore, the only true statement is that it follows zero-order kinetics.
